title: ARIA Properties & States: Making Widgets Talk 📢
description: Master aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-expanded, and more to communicate state.

slides.title: Naming Things: Accessible Name Computation 🏷️
slides.content:
Assistive tech needs to know what to **call** an element. The accessible name is computed from (in priority order):

1. `aria-labelledby` (references an element with text)
2. `aria-label` (a direct text string)
3. Native labelling (`<label>` for inputs, text content for buttons, `alt` for images)
4. `title` attribute (last resort, not recommended)

Use `aria-label` when no visible text label exists; use `aria-labelledby` when text exists elsewhere on the page.

quizData.question: Which attribute would you use to give a `<button>×</button>` an accessible name?
quizData.explanation: Since there's no visible text label to reference, `aria-label='Close'` is the best choice.

slides.title: Describing Things: aria-describedby 📝
slides.content:
`aria-describedby` links an element to additional descriptive text – like error messages or hints. * Unlike `aria-labelledby`, it does not replace the accessible name. * Screen readers read the name first, then may offer "press a key to hear description". Example: `` and `

Must be a valid address

`.

slides.title: Error Message Association
slides.codeSnippet: Please enter a valid email.

quizData.question: How does `aria-describedby` differ from `aria-labelledby`?

options.text: aria-describedby provides supplementary information; aria-labelledby provides the primary name

quizData.explanation: The accessible name comes from `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`; `aria-describedby` adds extra info.

slides.title: States That Change 🔄
slides.content:
* `aria-expanded` – true/false, indicates if a collapsible section is open.
* `aria-selected` – for selected items in a tablist or listbox.
* `aria-checked` – for custom checkboxes/radios (use native `<input>` instead).
* `aria-hidden` – hides an element from assistive tech (but not visually).

Always update these via JavaScript as the user interacts.

quizData.question: What state attribute would you use on a disclosure button that shows/hides a panel?

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Never Use aria-hidden on a Focusable Element
If an element has `aria-hidden="true"` but is in the tab order, users can focus something invisible to the screen reader – confusing and broken.
